summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate reports simulation_allowed=false, input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, and comparison_valid=false. The scenario is a custom 2D steady experiment type, but it has no blocks and no power_w object. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace, while the paper's observable is a 60 Hz, 52-minute workload-driven LSTM prediction on an Intel i5-3337U. The paper reports per-heat-source RMSE of 2.04 to 2.57 degC (HS#11 lowest, HS#10 highest, HS#1 at 2.36 degC) and an observed range of 58.73 to 101.35 degC. These are data-driven prediction errors, not outputs of a thermal solver, so a steady 2D solve would not correspond to them. There is no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace asset, no bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no generated placement. No source commit exists and no input.flp or input.ptrace was produced. No numerical comparison is made, since the Studio produced no temperatures and the location, aggregation, regime, and boundary assumptions do not match. Only qualitative sensitivity is discussed. The paper's cooling is a rear Peltier with a liquid-cooled hot side and a bare die facing the IR camera, whereas a Studio run would use default package assumptions. The result is a not-applicable verdict, and it must not be read as replication or validation of the paper.
limitations: The Studio did not run, so there are no simulated temperatures, no input.flp, and no input.ptrace.
The feasibility verdict is not_2d_applicable and comparison_valid is false, so no exact replication or numerical agreement can be claimed.
No floorplan geometry is published (no block x, y, width, height, and no die size), and the 18 heat-source centroids are only graphical in Fig. 8.
No per-block power in watts, no total chip power, no splitting rule, and no power time series or frequency and voltage operating point are published.

Observable mismatch: the paper's metric is the LSTM prediction RMSE per heat source (2.04 to 2.57 degC) on a held-out test set, which a thermal solver does not produce. The observed 58.73 to 101.35 degC range has no stated location or sample.
Regime mismatch: the paper is transient and workload-driven (60 Hz, 52 min, 187200 samples), while a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace.

Boundary mismatch: the Peltier and liquid-cooled hot side with a bare die differ from default Studio package, TIM, and heat spreader assumptions. Peltier setpoint, hot-side liquid temperature, and material conductivities are not published.
Evidence items 11 to 13 lack a valid page or pinned asset locator, there is no cited steady/transient regime, and the adversarial and independent review checks are unresolved or pending.

No pinned assets or linked repositories exist (artifact_search_status is checked_no_links). The only linked resource is the Intel PCM tool URL, which is not a floorplan or power input. Raw IR maps, the dataset, LSTM weights, and the training optimizer and loss function are unavailable.

Any future illustrative run would need generated coordinates and powers kept separate from paper facts, and its temperatures could not be compared numerically to the paper's RMSE or temperature range.

No floorplan geometry is published (no block x, y, width, height), and no per-block power in watts. The 18 heat-source centroids lack named blocks and dimensions, and the paper explicitly says it does not use the processor floorplan. A Studio 2D steady-state model cannot be built from the paper's facts, and this is essential.

Cooling mismatch: the experiment uses a rear-mounted Peltier/thermo-electric cooler with a liquid-cooled hot side, and the die front is exposed bare to the IR camera. There is no heat sink or package lid in the measurement, which differs from a typical heat-sink-based chip stack.

Transient and workload mismatch: the result is a dynamic, workload-driven LSTM prediction (60 Hz time series over 52 minutes). No steady-state power map or single operating point is published, so a steady 2D solve does not correspond to the paper's observable.

Solver mismatch: the paper uses data-driven LSTM regression and image processing, not a finite-difference or finite-element thermal solver. Only a simple COMSOL validation of the Laplacian idea is mentioned. A Studio solver would not reproduce the RMSE metric.

The paper reports no 3D stacking, interposer, chiplet, optimizer or reliability evaluation. Reliability (EM, BTI, HCI) is mentioned only as motivation. The die is a single commercial processor, so interposer and placement-optimizer features of the Studio package are not applicable.
No paper-derived floorplan exists, so any Studio run would use a separate illustrative 2D placement with generated coordinates, kept distinct from paper facts.

Any illustrative run would use the Studio's bundled default package and material assumptions (default die, TIM, heat spreader and boundary conditions). Their values were not supplied in the packet and are not paper-derived.
Total chip power cannot be split across blocks because the paper publishes no power or splitting rule. Any power would be a one-row illustrative trace, not paper data.
Temperatures from an illustrative Studio run must not be compared numerically to the paper's RMSE (2.04 to 2.57 degC) or temperature range.
